question.text: Which of the following is NOT a general pooling consideration for AIF structuring?

answer.text: The pool should have limited liability
The structure should maximize complexity to avoid regulatory scrutiny
Regulatory compliance with SEBI, FEMA, and RBI requirements

explanation.text: The Logic: The general pooling considerations listed in the workbook (pp. 100-101) include limited liability, tax neutrality, regulatory compliance, and avoiding overly complex structures. Designing complexity to evade scrutiny is the opposite of good practice and may attract GAAR examination. The Trap: Option C inverts the stated principle. Complex structures lacking commercial substance invite regulatory investigation rather than shielding the fund. Note: Additional guidance on investor simplicity or legitimate multi-jurisdiction complexity is not on the cited pooling-consideration pages and should be separately sourced before being treated as a workbook position.
